lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Implement state updates using a functional update in a counter.

Make sure to pick (prevCount) => prevCount + 1.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use a functional update. Calculate the next count from the callback's argument, adding one.

Make sure to pick setCount, followed by prevCount, and finally + 1.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which approach correctly implements functional updates in React?

setState((prev) => prev + 1)setState(state + 1)setState((state) + 1)setState((state) => state)

setState((prev) => prev + 1).
lessons.hardModeContent:
You call the same update twice in one event handler. Which update adds two in total to the numeric state?

setState((previous) => previous + 1)setState(state + 1)setState((state) + 1)setState((previous) => previous)

setState((previous) => previous + 1).

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Implement a component that updates the quote using useEffect.

Make sure to pick useEffect followed by () and then =>, {, }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use useEffect to replace the loading text with a quote.

Set the quote to To be, or not to be, that is the question.

Make sure to pick useEffect, followed by (), =>, setQuote, and finally "To be, or not to be, that is the question.".

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
In the following example code, what will the output be in the console after rendering?

RenderedHelloUpdatedNothing

Make sure to pick Rendered.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You render Message again without unmounting it. What does its effect do after this extra render?

It logs Rendered again.It logs nothing because effects only run on mount.It logs Hello React! from the paragraph.It logs Message, the component name.

It logs Rendered again.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Implement a simple counter using useEffect that logs to the console whenever the counter updates.

Make sure to type [count].

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
When does the cleanup function in useEffect run?

When the component unmountsWhen the component mountsWhen the component updatesEvery 10 seconds

When the component unmounts.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your effect has [] and returns a cleanup function.

The component mounts, renders again, then unmounts. When does the cleanup run?

Only when the component unmountsAfter the first render and again after the next renderOnly before the component first mountsOnly before the second render

Only when the component unmounts.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these statements is true about the useEffect hook's dependency array?

An empty dependency array means useEffect runs once on mountIt automatically cleans up the componentIt forces the component to unmountIt runs each time a functional component re-renders

An empty dependency array means useEffect runs once on mount.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A component uses useEffect(() => { loadProfile(); }, []). When does loadProfile run?

After the component first mountsAfter every renderOnly after loadProfile changesOnly when the component unmounts

After the component first mounts.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the useState hook to batch update a counter and log the number of clicks on a button.

Make sure to type setClicks.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
How does batching state updates benefit performance in React?

By reducing the number of re-rendersBy increasing the number of render cyclesBy making state updates synchronousBy using more memory

By reducing the number of re-renders.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A click handler makes several state updates. Why can React batch those updates before rendering?

It can avoid rendering separately for each update.It makes every state value update immediately.It reruns the component once for every update.It stores more copies of each state value.

It can avoid rendering separately for each update.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the correct hook to set a new color after every re-render of the application.

Make sure to type useEffect.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which array of dependencies will cause useEffect to run every time the score variable changes?

[score][count][][setScore]

Make sure to pick [score].
lessons.hardModeContent:
An effect reads score and should run again only when that value changes. Which dependency array belongs with it?

[score][count][][total]

Make sure to pick [score].

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the purpose of the dependency array in the useEffect hook?

To determine when to re-run the effectTo store data fetched from APIsTo log the errors during a fetchTo style the component differently

To determine when to re-run the effect.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A component fetches results whenever its query changes. What job does the dependency array perform in this effect?

It tells React to rerun the effect when listed values change.It stores the fetched results for the component.It logs fetch errors automatically.It applies CSS styles after the fetch.

It tells React to rerun the effect when listed values change.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Modify the useEffect hook to log a message when the component mounts and unmounts using a cleanup function.

Make sure to pick return followed by () => and then console.log("Component Unmounted");, , []).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Modify the useEffect hook to log a message when the component mounts and unmounts using a cleanup function. Complete the cleanup that logs Component Unmounted, then make the effect mount-only.

Make sure to pick useEffect, followed by return, () =>, "Component Unmounted", and finally [].
